The applicant vide the present application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 [CrPC] seeks anticipatory bail in FIR No.001/2021 dated 01.01.2021 under Section 409/420/120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [IPC] at PS. Economic Offences Wing, Delhi.
2. The FIR was registered on the complaint made by one Arvind Kumar, a Director of ARC Infraheights Private Limited which is engaged in the business of earthing, mining and construction.
As per FIR, one Sh. Sanoj Bhati introduced the complainant to the applicant namely Avnindra This is a digitally signed order.

3.

sentences.text: However, due to some technical problem, the said tender could not be worked out.
The complainant was then offered another tender for mining work in Azgarpur, Noida, Uttar Pradesh and was induced to pay further Rs.3.25 Crores.
The complainant transferred the said amount of Rs.3.25 Crores from time to time i.e. from 09.01.2018 till May, 2018 into the bank account of G&MIPL.
Resultantly, the complainant paid a total amount of Rs.4.20 Crores approx. to the accused persons.

4. Further, as per FIR, Raghvendra Dubey, a co-accused, met the complainant at Bihar Niwas,
Chanakyapuri, Delhi regarding 'sand mining' tender and introduced himself as the authorized signatory of G&MIPL and assured the complainant regarding the work.
However, as nothing happened further despite the complainant making repeated requests, the present FIR came to be registered on the basis of his complaint.

5. Learned senior counsel appearing for the applicant submits that the applicant herein has been falsely implicated in the present case by the complainant as the accused/applicant never intended to cheat the

She submits that the same is evident from the fact that the applicant's company had made investments to the tune of Rs.4.10 Crores (approx.) before the complainant approached him for an investment in the project.

She further submits that around June, 2019, due to some dispute inter-se the applicant's company and the Government of Uttar Pradesh, the Project was in a limbo,
and when the complainant asked for money.

As the applicant's company failed to return the complainant's investment, the complainant filed a complaint with PS Timarpur, Delhi which was sent to Economic Offences Wing, Delhi and converted into the impugned FIR.
In view of the above submissions, the learned senior counsel submits that the present is a case of a business transaction gone sour, which is being given a criminal colour.
6. The learned senior counsel for the applicant further submits that the present FIR came to be registered only on 01.01.2021, while the project at Asgarpur was brought to halt on 03.10.2019.
She submits that the same highlights that the present FIR is only a pressure tactic being used by the complainant.
7. Notice was issued and the Status Report was also called.
8. Learned APP appearing for the State opposes the application in light of the fact that the investigation is underway and custodial interrogation of the applicant is required.
She further submits that the applicant is also named in two other FIRs, where investigation is underway.

Lastly,
she submits that in light of a complex money trail and the involvement of large sums of money,
custodial interrogation of the applicant is quintessential.

She also submits that their existed an intention to cheat from the inception which is evident from the fact that the applicant had not paid the royalties, leading to the cancellation of the mining lease.

She further submits that it is an admitted fact that the complainant had paid Rs.3,20,00,000/- and Rs.1,00,00,000/- via bank transfer and in cash respectively, to the companies of the accused persons.
She also submits that an amount of Rs.1,00,00,000/- was returned to the complainant only after registration of the present FIR.

She lastly submits that the applicant herein is inexplicably involved in the offence as he received the amount in his account, and grant of anticipatory bail would lead to hampering of investigation and influencing of witnesses.
10. This Court has heard the learned senior counsel(s) for the applicant and the complainant and the learned APP for the State and perused the documents on record.
11. Facts borne out reflect that, admittedly, the complainant invested in the companies of the accused persons upon coming to know of the accused persons from someone else.

Facts also reveal that the complainant invested a total sum of Rs.4.20 Crores in the companies of the accused persons between 11.12.2017 to May, 2018 and the applicant's company was granted a mining lease during the same time i.e. on 23.04.2018.

Facts also reveal that by then the applicant had already spent an amount of more than Rs.4 Crores towards Royalty to the Government of Uttar Pradesh in addition to around Rs.65 Lakhs towards various investments/ salaries etc.
12.
Further, admittedly, G&MIPL, one of the companies of the accused persons, has already returned an amount of Rs.1,00,00,000/- Crore in
This is a digitally signed order.

An additional sum of Rs.80 Lakhs was also paid to the complainant as recorded in an earlier order dated 24.05.2023 of this Court in the present proceedings.

13. Further, in view of this Court, at the stage of granting anticipatory bail to the applicant, it would be premature for this Court to come to a conclusion that there was/ is an element of mala fide on the part of the applicant.

14. It is also pertinent to note that the transactions involving the parties are documentary in nature which can be called for/ produced as and when required at any stage for which custodial interrogation is not required.

However, the pendency of any other proceedings against the applicant cannot bar this Court from allowing the present application for grant of anticipatory bail.
16. Furthermore, it is a matter of fact that the applicant has since joined the investigation on 12.08.2023 and is also expected to co-operate with the investigation henceforth.

17. This Court wishes to take note of the fact that in numerous cases pending trail, unfortunately there is a recent growing trend wherein an applicant, despite either making a statement through counsel in the Court or despite conditions imposed by the Court, chooses merely to 'physically' join investigation on paper without any cooperation, assistance or actual This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/11/2023 at 21:53:32 participation.

This Court deprecates the same as an applicant once granted bail has to meaningfully,
not only join but by all means participate therein.
Lest the purpose of granting bail, more so that of granting anticipatory bail, to an accused will be defeated and it shall cause a hindrance to the investigation being carried on.

The applicant is expected to show high sensitivity, diligence and understand, not only the purpose but also the consequences, of any unmeaningful participation and/ or non-compliance of the conditions imposed by the Court.
It is clarified that the applicant is not only to join the investigation but also has to participate therein for onward and effective investigation to continue and culminate after that.

18. As the aforesaid transaction inter-se the applicant and the complainant was for a particular purpose for which the applicant had already made a substantial contribution/ investment and both the applicant and the complainant are in businesses involving commercial transaction(s) as also the applicant has already returned a cumulative sum of Rs.1.8 Crores to the complainant, without going into the merits of the matter, in the opinion of this Court, it prima facie deems to be a fit case for granting anticipatory bail to the applicant.
19. Accordingly, the applicant is granted anticipatory bail in FIR No.001/2021 dated 01.01.2021 under Section 409/420/120B IPC at PS Economic Offences Wing, Delhi.

In the event of the arrest of the applicant, he shall be released after furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/-
[Rupees Two Lakh Only] alongwith one surety of the like amount by a family member/ friend having no criminal case pending against them, subject to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court,
